claim: Existing uncertainty scores for LLMs are often heuristic: choosing a threshold on such a score does not by itself provide statistical guarantees on the error rate among accepted (non-abstained) answers.
stance_target: the calibration disconnect: raw uncertainty scores alone are not trustworthy decision-making signals without further calibration machinery
quoted_support: existing uncertainty scores for LLMs are often heuristic: a threshold chosen on such scores does not, by itself, provide statistical guarantees on the error rate among accepted answers.

claim: CIC converts an ARBITRARY uncertainty score into a risk-controlled selective-answering rule by using a held-out calibration set to compute a high-probability upper confidence bound (Hoeffding or Clopper-Pearson) on the acceptance-conditioned error rate for each candidate threshold, then selecting the largest threshold whose bound stays below a user-set risk level alpha.
stance_target: a generic post-hoc wrapper can turn any uncertainty signal, well-calibrated or not, into a provably risk-controlled action -- directly applicable to wrapping a near-perfectly-calibrated sampling confidence signal
scope_conditions: requires exchangeability assumption and a held-out calibration set
quoted_support: For each candidate uncertainty threshold, CIC estimates the acceptance-conditioned error rate and constructs a high-probability upper confidence bound using either Hoeffding-style or Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals. It then selects the largest threshold whose upper bound is below a user-specified risk level alpha.

claim: Under exchangeability, CIC guarantees with probability at least 1-delta that the selected threshold controls the error rate among accepted answers at level alpha, and the method was validated on closed- and open-ended QA benchmarks across seven LLMs and multiple uncertainty estimators.
stance_target: feasibility of formally-guaranteed selective answering across diverse uncertainty estimator types
scope_conditions: seven LLMs, multiple uncertainty estimators, closed- and open-ended QA (general domain, not code)
quoted_support: Under exchangeability, CIC guarantees with probability at least 1-delta that the selected threshold, if non-null, controls the error rate among accepted answers at level alpha.

claim: CIC has not been applied to code generation or to repeated-sampling/self-consistency confidence signals specifically, leaving open whether wrapping a near-perfectly-calibrated sampling-based code confidence signal in this risk-control machinery yields a stronger accuracy-coverage tradeoff than existing code-specific abstention methods.
stance_target: gap: CIC-style risk control has not been combined with the target paper's near-perfectly-calibrated sampling signal for code
scope_conditions: inferred from abstract scope (general QA, not code)
quoted_support: We evaluate CIC on both closed-ended and open-ended QA benchmarks across seven LLMs and multiple uncertainty estimators.
